opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. If you wish to claim

opportunities.title: [MCP] HTTP proxy support for Remote MCP behind corporate firewalls
opportunities.summary: ## Context mcp-remote provides `--enable-proxy` to respect `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables. MisakaNet Remote MCP has no proxy awareness — agents behind corporate firewalls cannot reach `misakanet.org/mcp`. ## Why - Enterprise adoption: many corporate environments require HTTP proxy for outbound connections - China mainland: some networks need proxy to reach Cloudflare CDN reliably - Self-hosted: users running MisakaNet Worker on internal networks may need proxy for KV/GitHub API ## Proposed design For the Cloudflare Worker (server-side): not applicable — Workers run on Cloudflare edge, no proxy needed. For client-side integration (agents, CLI, SDK): 1. Document `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` support in README 2. In `misaka capture` CLI and any future SDK, respect proxy env vars: ```python import urllib.request proxy = os.environ.get("HTTPS_PROXY") or os.environ.get("HTTP_PROXY") if proxy: handler = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({"https": proxy}) opener = urllib.request.build_opener(handler) ``` 3. For MCP client config (Claude Desktop, Cursor): document proxy setup in troubleshooting ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] README troubleshooting section covers proxy setup - [ ]

opportunities.title: [bounty $400] Implement ABNF-compliant email address parser with full §3.2–§4.4 coverage
opportunities.summary: `source.md` contains the complete RFC 5322 specification (Internet Message Format). We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. This parser must handle every edge case defined in the RFC — not just simple `user@domain` patterns, but the full complexity of quoted strings, comments, folding whitespace, group addresses, and domain literals. ## Background RFC 5322 defines email address syntax through a chain of ABNF productions that build on each other: ``` address = mailbox / group mailbox = name-addr / addr-spec name-addr = [display-name] angle-addr angle-addr = [CFWS] "<" addr-spec ">" [CFWS] addr-spec = local-part "@" domain local-part = dot-atom / quoted-string / obs-local-part domain = dot-atom / domain-literal / obs-domain ``` Each of these references further productions (CFWS, FWS, quoted-pair, dtext, etc.) that span multiple sections. **You must read `source.md` completely** to trace the full grammar dependency chain. ## Requirements ### 1. Parser Implementation — `parser.py` ```python class RFC5322Address: """Parsed RFC 5322 email address.""" display_name
